title: Inference maintenance windows and fallback rights exhibit (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This exhibit captures proposed contractual language and operational expectations for scheduled and emergency maintenance of Redwood inference services (hosted, dedicated, and private). It covers notification timing, permissible maintenance windows, customer rights to failover or pause billing during extended maintenance, required fallback model behavior, and audit/evidence obligations.

Status and scope:
- Draft for legal and product review.
- Focused on inference endpoints (text generation, chat, embeddings) and associated routing/caching subsystems.
- Includes special considerations for Dedicated and Private deployments (customer-managed infra).

Key definitions (for contract text):
- "Maintenance": any planned activity that may degrade, suspend, or change the functional behavior or performance characteristics of a service or endpoint for the purpose of updates, patching, capacity changes, or migrations.
- "Emergency Maintenance": unscheduled maintenance required to address security incidents, data corruption, or severe outages.
- "Fallback Model": an alternative model variant or serving mode (lower concurrency, smaller model, quantized profile) Redwood will route traffic to when the primary model is unavailable to meet latency/cost SLOs.
- "Maintenance Window": time period during which Maintenance may be performed. Windows may differ by customer tier and geography.

Core exhibit proposals (contract clause language examples):
1) Planned maintenance notification and scheduling
- Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' advance written notice for Planned Maintenance affecting customer production endpoints. Notice will include: expected window start/end, estimated user impact (latency and availability), fallback behavior, and rollback plan.
- For Dedicated customers, notice may be reduced to 48 hours if customer has agreed to a separate maintenance schedule in the service order.
- Customers may request an alternative window within 24 hours of notice; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate requests that do not materially impact rollout safety.

2) Maintenance windows and permissible hours
- Default window: 02:00–07:00 UTC weekdays for hosted customers, unless a customer's traffic profile requires a different agreed-upon window.
- For enterprise customers requiring stricter controls (Private/Dedicated), maintenance scheduling will be coordinated through the customer's technical contact and a mutually-agreed calendar.

3) Emergency maintenance and accelerated notifications
- In cases of Emergency Maintenance that are necessary to remediate a material security vulnerability or to prevent imminent service degradation, Redwood may perform work without prior notice but will notify the customer as soon as practicable.
- If Emergency Maintenance results in customer-visible data exposure or significant service disruption, Redwood will follow the Incident Notification Timeline (see linked artifacts) and provide a post-incident remediation report within 10 business days.

4) Fallback rights and required behavior
- When a Primary Model becomes unavailable during or outside Maintenance windows, Redwood will route requests to a pre-configured Fallback Model that: (a) uses a smaller or compatible architecture; (b) preserves customer data segregation and encryption; (c) is announced in the notice; and (d) may have different latency/quality characteristics explicitly disclosed.
- Customers may opt out of automatic fallback on a per-endpoint basis (e.g., to fail closed) via configuration in the Console. If opted out, Redwood will reasonably attempt to maintain service but is not required to provide fallback.

5) Billing and crediting for prolonged/unplanned unavailable periods
- If an endpoint is unavailable for >4 consecutive hours outside of an agreed maintenance window and no fallback is available, customer may request downtime credit equal to pro rata fees for the affected period, capped at 100% of fees for the month of the incident.
- For Dedicated contracts with reserved capacity, emergency maintenance that results in >12 cumulative hours of capacity unavailability in a billing cycle triggers a review and potential service credit as defined in the service order.

6) Data handling and caching during maintenance
- Redwood will preserve KV and prefix caches where operationally feasible. When caches are purged for maintenance, Redwood will disclose whether any query logs, ephemeral logs, or KV snapshots were persisted to longer-term storage and provide the retention window.
- For Private deployments where customer-managed storage is used, Redwood will document operations and provide a signed evidence package describing cache flushes and any data movement.

7) Rollback, canary, and test practices
- Major maintenance (model upgrades, quantization changes) will be deployed via staged canaries with automated rollback triggers for quality, latency, or error-rate regressions.
- Contractual language: Redwood will ensure that rollouts impacting customer endpoints include a rollback plan and a canary period where the customer may request immediate rollback if regression thresholds are breached.

8) Audit and evidence obligations
- Following maintenance that affects customer data segregation or persistent logs, Redwood will provide an evidence packet (date/timestamps, engineer runbook entries, change-ids, truncated logs) within 7 business days upon request. Sensitive material may be redacted; Redwood will cooperate to provide attestation to the extent permitted by law and internal security policy.

9) Private and on-prem considerations
- For Private deployments where the customer controls the compute, Redwood's Maintenance is limited to software shipped to the customer. The exhibit should require advance coordination and that Redwood provides safe upgrade artifacts (signed binaries, checksums, migration scripts) and an operations runbook for customer execution.
- If Redwood requires on-prem access to perform maintenance (remote ops), specific credentials, access windows, and evidence collection procedures must be agreed in writing.

10) Service behavior during partial capacity degradation
- If Redwood detects reduced capacity that may impact latency (e.g., node failure, GPU offload), traffic will be routed according to the customer's routing policy: latency-first, cost-first, or strict-isolation. Customers may update routing policy in Console or via API.
- Contractual fallback exhibit should enumerate routing policies and default to "latency-first" unless otherwise specified.

Open items and questions (for legal/product):
- Credit caps for multi-tenant hosted customers vs Dedicated customers: should Dedicated credits be higher or trigger different remedies?
- Exact evidence format for cache flushes — CSV manifest vs signed hash blobs? (ops preference: signed manifest + runbook excerpt)
- Opt-out mechanics for automatic fallback — should opt-out require additional indemnities or limitations?
- Harmonize Emergency Maintenance notification timelines with existing Incident Response playbook.

Example short clause to insert into DPA or SOW:
"Maintenance and Fallback Exhibit: Provider will schedule Planned Maintenance to minimize production impact and will provide at least 72 hours notice for such maintenance. Provider will maintain Fallback Models to preserve availability; Customer may elect to opt out of fallback for sensitive workloads. In the event the Service is unavailable for more than four continuous hours outside an agreed maintenance window and no fallback is provided, Customer may request a pro rata credit. Provider will provide an evidence packet for any maintenance event that affects persistent customer data within seven business days on request."

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- Product: confirm realistic default maintenance windows per region; verify whether 72/48-hour splits are operationally achievable.
- Legal: prefer shorter or longer notification windows? consider market precedent.
- SRE/ops: attach runbook snippets and a sample evidence packet template.

Change log:

Unresolved: need alignment with existing SLA exhibit templates and the Incident Response timeline.

End of draft.
